reading.body:
Japan's only listed AI data center in this dataset is the JERA Chiba facility in Chiba, operated by RHAELM.

The record is a single facility, so it describes a starting point rather than a buildout. It places one AI data center in Japan and names its operator, but it carries no capacity figure, no power draw, no grid connection, and no construction date. Nothing here shows whether the site is operating, permitted, or announced.

For AI specifically, a data center is only as real as the power and the building behind it. A name and a city do not establish either. The dataset cannot say how much compute this facility supports, what it draws from the grid, or how it compares to any other site.

What it does not cover is most of the question. There is no count of Japan's total AI data centers, no timeline, and no link between this facility and the chips or models it might serve. Treat it as one confirmed entry, not as a measure of Japan's AI infrastructure.
